note: Clamped posterior (0.72 dominant), non-reasoning model, N=3, 2 prompts. 30 configurations (5 modes x gate x monologue with strategy = 20, plus 10 strategy-stripped with monologue off); 180 replies total. Partial factorial: strategy-off x monologue-on not run. Words per reply. (v1.0 wrote '180 cells' -- that counted replies.)
reading: Under a STRONG clamped posterior the mode predicts reply behaviour (mode-conditioned style; strategy line ON, so largely instruction following -- not a probabilistic calibration test). The strategy line disciplines/shortens strongly; the gate token moves length SUBSTANTIALLY and non-uniformly (disengaging 133.5->56, asserting 46->78; v1.0 called this 'modest' -- corrected); the monologue shortens the longest states but lengthens asserting (46->65.5), so its effect is selective. Corrects e1: bare state numbers are NOT universally inert -- that was a weak-state artefact.
control_naming_note: The key 'numbers_only' is retained for data continuity but the control is STRATEGY-STRIPPED, not numbers-only: its prefix still carries all mode names and values, the 'Dominant <mode>, gate=<...>' fields and 'Treat this as internal stance.' 'gate off' inserts gate=full scope (not absence). The monologue condition also appends 'Act on that assessment.'
